whatItDoes: A Node CLI (whose-earth.mjs) plus a page that hold a 94-row registry of every line in Aster and Skyhook stating Earth's mu, radius, g0, rotation speed or a reboost energy per kg, re-verify each row's file:line against both checkouts and scan both repos for unlisted occurrences (failing on drift), then build each program's Earth from those rows. It recomputes every Earth-dependent rev_a.json value on each Earth (Skyhook mu 398,600/R 6,371 vs Aster 398,600.4418/R 6,378.137), sizes the K2 interface effects (C3 shift +0.0290/+0.0267/+0.0213 km^2/s^2 consistent, +0.1066 mixed, mu alone -0.000037; cislunar apogee +5,730 km; v-inf* 3.6127->3.6156; Aster injection -0.5 to -0.6 m/s), and reconciles reboost energy (finance 2*v_orb*v_tip = 37.78 MJ/kg vs orbital energy 43.03 vs MP-001 44.8, which none of 144 readings of the canon reproduces; the decision grid's reboost line reproduces 9/9 at 4 dp only as 2*v_orb*v_tip on R 6,371). Missing constants are structured refusals (Aster has no Earth rotation rate; GTO/TLI thresholds need a target radius).

deviationsFromProposal: (a) The C3 shift under R = 6378.137 is 0.021-0.029 km^2/s^2 when each side is self-consistent; the proposal's ~0.11 (1.3% of -8.06) holds only for the mixed reading (v_orb from one Earth, r_tip from the other), as judge 3 noted; both are computed and tested, and the proposal's 0.10-0.12 band is applied to the mixed reading only. (b) The proposal's candidate explanation for 44.8 MJ/kg does not reproduce it: adding the 290->930 km potential term gives 43.03, plus the ground-relative catch gives 45.27; a 144-reading sweep finds nothing that rounds to 44.8; reported as unexplained. (c) Citations corrected: INV-025 is the public-copy taxonomy rule (INVARIANTS.md:199), the relevant invariant is INV-026 (:200); INV-021 (frame-by-measurement) applies only by analogy. (d) Scope widened where the question led: 94 registry rows instead of five constants in two places, a scan that fails on unlisted occurrences, Aster's own published injection values as pins, and the decision grid plus three workbook rows because that is where 37.78 MJ/kg reaches a published number. (e) Data: 10 snapshots (26 KB with sidecars) rather than 2, because the arithmetic also reads physics-module literals, Aster's parking altitude and g0, the pins' text, workbook rows and grid; the 70 citation-only rows are verified live and recorded in data.js instead of being snapshotted file by file, to keep du -sk under 500. (f) Recomputing the canon overlaps idea 04's --verify-canon; the new part is the second and third Earth. (g) Surface: CLI as specified, plus an index.html page (Earth picker, filterable concordance) that runs the same model.
notBuilt: No full K2 interface envelope (idea 01 already builds one; K1 return-leg v-inf does not exist in Aster). Market-threshold tip speeds for GTO (2.1) and TLI (2.8) are refused, not recomputed, because rev_a.json states no GEO radius or lunar distance. The ground-relative lower-tip speed on Aster's Earth is refused (Aster states no rotation rate). The source of MP-001's 44.8 MJ/kg was not found; the sweep shows only that the obvious readings of the canon do not give it, not that none could. The orbital-energy accounting is an energy bound under the canon's rigid-rotation, no-dissipation model; electrodynamic restoration of energy and angular momentum together is not modelled, and no payback/NPV effect of the reboost difference was computed (only $/kg on the published grid line). The origin of Aster's 6,371.010 km render radius was not traced. Offline (no checkouts), 70 of 94 rows are shown from the saved run in data.js rather than re-verified, and the scan cannot run. Not through Aster's multi-agent math audit, oracle validation, DEC process or protected-core review, nor Skyhook's Rule 1 canon review, a VM, or its pytest suite (pytest not installed; Python tests are unittest).
